slots.practicalActivity: Install Power BI Desktop from the Microsoft Store or powerbi.microsoft.com, then spend 20 minutes clicking through every ribbon tab (Home, Insert, Modeling, View, Help) and the three view icons (Report/Data/Model) without opening a file yet, just to build a mental map of where things live.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed working install of Power BI Desktop, plus a short written note (3-4 bullet points) describing what Get Data, Transform, Model, Visualize, and Publish each do.

lessons.title: The Power BI Workflow: Get → Transform → Model → Visualize → Publish

slots.practicalActivity: Download Microsoft's built-in 'Financial Sample.xlsx' (Get Data > Excel, search 'power bi financial sample download' if not bundled) and build your first report: load it, drag Sales and Country onto a bar chart, add a card showing total Profit, and add a slicer for Segment.
slots.deliverable: A saved .pbix file ('01-first-report.pbix') containing one bar chart, one card, and one working slicer built from the Financial Sample data.

slots.practicalActivity: Connect to two different source types from the Get Data menu: open the Financial Sample as an Excel source, then export one of its sheets to CSV and reconnect to that CSV file, comparing how the Source step in Power Query differs between the two.
slots.deliverable: One .pbix with two separate queries loaded ('FinancialSample_Excel' and 'FinancialSample_CSV') and a one-paragraph note comparing the Source step generated for each.

lessons.title: Connecting to Web, JSON & REST API Data

slots.practicalActivity: If SQL Server with a sample database (e.g. AdventureWorks2012) is available, connect to one table via Get Data > SQL Server; if not, connect to a free public JSON API (e.g. https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users) via Get Data > Web. For whichever connection you made, decide and justify Import vs. DirectQuery for that source.
slots.deliverable: A working query against either a SQL table or a REST API endpoint, plus a written Import/DirectQuery decision with reasoning specific to that source.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Financial Sample query in Power Query Editor and walk through every step in the Query Settings pane. Then manually fix the data type of at least 5 columns (e.g. force Date to Date, Units Sold to Whole Number, Gross Sales to Fixed Decimal) and watch the step list update as you go.
slots.deliverable: A query with your own 'Changed Type' step, and a written list of the data type you assigned to each of the 5 columns and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Remove rows where Units Sold is blank or zero, filter out one Country of your choosing, then introduce a deliberate text error (type a letter into a numeric-looking cell in a copy of the source Excel file) and practice using Replace Values and Replace Errors to resolve it.
slots.deliverable: A cleaned query with explicit 'Removed Rows', 'Filtered Rows', and 'Replaced Errors' steps visible in the Applied Steps list.

slots.practicalActivity: Split the 'Country' column on a delimiter in a throwaway copy, extract the first 3 characters of 'Product' into a new column, then add a Conditional Column that labels each row 'High Margin' or 'Low Margin' based on a Gross Margin threshold you pick yourself.
slots.deliverable: A query with one split/extracted text column and one conditional column, with your margin threshold and labeling logic noted in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Duplicate the query, pivot the 'Month Name' column into separate columns of summed Sales, then unpivot it back to confirm the round-trip. Separately, use Group By to build a new summary table of total Sales and average Profit per Country.
slots.deliverable: A standalone summary query ('Sales_By_Country') produced via Group By, kept separate from your main fact query.

slots.practicalActivity: Split the Financial Sample into two mock year-range tables in Excel, load both, and Append them back into one stacked table. Separately, build a small Country-to-Region lookup table and Merge it into your main query as a new Region column.
slots.deliverable: One appended combined-years query and one merged query with a new 'Region' column pulled from a separate lookup table.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Power Query Parameter (e.g. a MinUnitsSold threshold) and wire it into a filter step so changing the parameter changes which rows load. Then review every query you've built so far: rename cryptic step names, set staging queries to 'disable load', and check where query folding is breaking.
slots.deliverable: A working parameter that changes filtered results when edited, plus a cleaned-up set of queries with renamed steps and non-essential queries set to not load.

slots.practicalActivity: Drill: load a different public dataset you haven't used yet (e.g. a sample orders export CSV) and, in one sitting, use a parameter to drive a filter on it, then wrap a column-by-column note of which Power Query feature from this chapter you'd reach for to fix three deliberately messy columns you pick yourself (a text/number mismatch, a blank-heavy column, and a column that needs splitting).
slots.deliverable: One parameterized query against a new dataset, plus a written 3-item plan mapping messy columns to the specific Power Query feature that fixes each.

slots.practicalActivity: Without following lesson-by-lesson instructions, take a different raw public dataset (e.g. a sample orders export CSV) and independently chain at least 6 Power Query techniques from this chapter: a data type fix, row filtering, a conditional column, a merge with a lookup table, a group-by summary, and a parameter, choosing the order yourself.
slots.deliverable: An original cleaned query, built from a dataset you chose, demonstrating at least 6 distinct Power Query techniques chained together end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the Financial Sample data plus the Region lookup table from Chapter 3, classify each table in writing as a fact table or a dimension table, then arrange them in Model view so the fact table sits centered with dimension tables around it, approximating a star schema.
slots.deliverable: A written fact/dimension classification for at least 3 tables and a Model view layout with the fact table centered and dimension tables arranged around it.

slots.practicalActivity: In Model view, draw a relationship from your Region lookup table to the fact table on the Country key, explicitly check and set its cardinality, then toggle cross-filter direction from single to both to see the visual change before deciding which direction is correct and reverting if needed.
slots.deliverable: A working relationship with cardinality and filter direction set deliberately (not left on Power BI's auto-detected default), plus a one-sentence written justification for your final choice.

lessons.title: Building a Complete Power BI Data Model

slots.practicalActivity: Create a second relationship between two tables already connected elsewhere (forcing it to become inactive), inspect it in Model view, then finish a complete model with at least 3 dimension tables connected to your one fact table.
slots.deliverable: A complete data model in the .pbix Model view with one fact table, at least 3 dimension tables, and one active plus one inactive relationship clearly visible.

slots.practicalActivity: Start a new .pbix, import a fresh dataset with at least 3 naturally related tables (e.g. orders, customers, products from any free sample retail dataset), and build a complete star schema from scratch: classify fact vs. dimension tables, create all relationships, and set cardinality and filter direction deliberately for each.
slots.deliverable: A new .pbix ('04-model-review.pbix') with an original, correctly structured star schema model built without lesson-by-lesson guidance.

slots.practicalActivity: In your Chapter 4 model, open a new measure and type 3 original DAX expressions from scratch (not copied from the lesson): a literal-number measure, a simple SUM measure, and a measure with an explanatory // comment.
slots.deliverable: 3 original, working measures demonstrating correct DAX syntax (table/column referencing, a comment) that you wrote without copying the lesson's examples.

slots.practicalActivity: Create one calculated column on your fact table (e.g. a row-by-row Profit Margin % column) and one measure that aggregates something different (e.g. Average Order Value), using your own field names and logic rather than the lesson's worked example.
slots.deliverable: One calculated column and one measure, both using original naming and a calculation not identical to the lesson's example, validated in a table visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Without referring back to the lesson, write 5 new measures from scratch against your model: Total Sales, Total Units, Average Order Value, Distinct Customer Count, and Max Single-Order Profit.
slots.deliverable: 5 original measures added to the model, each tested in a table visual to confirm the values look correct.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short explanation in your own words of why a calculated column recalculates per row at refresh while a measure recalculates per filter context at query time. Then build 2 new aggregation measures using COUNTROWS and DISTINCTCOUNT on columns you choose that haven't been used yet.
slots.deliverable: A short written comparison plus 2 new aggregation measures (not duplicating earlier ones), validated in a visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a matrix visual by Country and Year, then write an original CALCULATE measure of your own design (e.g. 'Sales for one specific Country regardless of the row's own Country') to directly observe filter context being overridden next to a plain SUM measure.
slots.deliverable: A working CALCULATE-based measure shown in a matrix beside a plain SUM measure, with a written note on which filter it overrides and why the numbers differ.

slots.practicalActivity: Drill practice: write 4 original CALCULATE measures, each overriding a different filter (one by Country, one by Year, one by Segment, and one combining two conditions with AND logic inside CALCULATE), and place all 4 side by side in one table visual to compare results.
slots.deliverable: A table visual showing 4 distinct CALCULATE-based measures with visibly different, explainable results, none copied from the lesson's formula.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a calculated column that references a measure to trigger context transition, write down what value you expected versus what you got and why, then write 2 original SUMX measures (e.g. a weighted-profit calculation and a custom row-level calculation not shown in the lesson).
slots.deliverable: One demonstrated context-transition example with a written explanation, plus 2 original SUMX measures cross-checked against a manual spot-check.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 original measures using CALCULATE filter modifiers (one with KEEPFILTERS, one with REMOVEFILTERS/ALL on a specific column) and one original measure using FILTER() to build a table filter expression (e.g. 'Sales for orders above the average order value'), using your own thresholds.
slots.deliverable: 3 original measures (2 filter-modifier, 1 FILTER-based), each validated in a card or table visual with sensible, explainable numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: Timed drill: in 45 minutes, write 6 new measures combining iterators and FILTER with no lesson reference — for example 'Average Profit Margin for high-value orders only' or 'Total Units for a specific Segment using FILTER instead of CALCULATE's implicit filter'. Check each against a manually calculated expected value in a second table visual.
slots.deliverable: 6 original measures built under time pressure, each cross-checked against an independently calculated expected value.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original ALL-based measure (e.g. a '% of Total Sales' using SUM divided by an ALL-wrapped SUM) and an original ALLEXCEPT measure (e.g. a subtotal that ignores everything except Country), then build a visual showing an ALLSELECTED measure behaving differently from the ALL measure once a slicer is applied.
slots.deliverable: 3 original measures (ALL, ALLEXCEPT, ALLSELECTED) in one visual, with a written note on the specific case where ALLSELECTED's result differs from ALL's.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick your 3 messiest measures from this chapter and refactor them using VAR/RETURN for readability and to avoid repeated calculations, following DAX naming best practices.
slots.deliverable: 3 refactored measures using VAR/RETURN that produce identical results to their original versions, confirmed side by side in a visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a 'measure library' table visual listing every measure you've written this chapter (15+) with its result for the current filter context, then clean up the Fields pane by deleting or organizing unused test measures into display folders.
slots.deliverable: An organized measure library visual plus a trimmed Fields pane with unused test measures removed or filed into folders.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, design and build 5 brand-new DAX measures for a business question you invent yourself (e.g. 'what is our profit concentration risk?'), using at least one CALCULATE, one iterator function, and one ALL-family function across the 5 measures combined.
slots.deliverable: 5 original business-driven measures covering CALCULATE, an iterator function, and an ALL-family function, in a single summary visual with a one-paragraph explanation of the business question each answers.

slots.practicalActivity: Build your own Date table using CALENDAR or CALENDARAUTO (typed yourself, not copy-pasted), mark it as a Date table in Model view, add Year/Month Name/Quarter calculated columns, and relate it to your fact table's order date.
slots.deliverable: A marked Date table joined to the fact table, with Year, Month Name, and Quarter calculated columns you wrote yourself.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original DATEADD measure comparing Sales to the same period last year, then write 3 original time-intelligence measures of your own (YTD Sales, MTD Units, QTD Profit) using your Date table.
slots.deliverable: 4 original time-intelligence measures (1 DATEADD-based, 3 YTD/MTD/QTD) shown correctly in a line chart with a date-axis slicer.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original measure using DATESYTD or TOTALYTD with a custom fiscal year-end date different from the lesson's example, and one measure using DATESBETWEEN for a specific custom date range relevant to your dataset.
slots.deliverable: 2 original measures (one fiscal-YTD, one DATESBETWEEN range) validated against manually counted expected values for a known date range.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a single 'Time Intelligence Dashboard' page combining your Chapter 6 measures: a line chart of YTD Sales vs. prior-year YTD, a card showing QTD Profit, and a slicer that lets you pick any year to confirm every measure still recalculates correctly.
slots.deliverable: A working dashboard page where changing the year slicer correctly recalculates every time-intelligence measure without errors.

slots.practicalActivity: For 3 different business questions (trend over time, comparison across categories, single KPI), choose and justify a visual type for each in writing, then build a Table and a Matrix visual showing Sales by Country and Year with subtotals enabled.
slots.deliverable: A written justification for 3 visual-type choices, plus a working Table and Matrix visual with subtotals enabled.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one bar chart, one line chart, and one pie chart using different field combinations than any lesson example, then add a Card showing a KPI you pick and a Slicer that filters all 3 charts at once.
slots.deliverable: A report page with 3 distinct chart types plus a card and slicer, all cross-filtering correctly when the slicer is used.

slots.practicalActivity: Apply conditional formatting to a table (e.g. a color scale on Profit Margin, icons on a performance column) using thresholds you set yourself, then configure the Filter pane to add one visual-level filter and one page-level filter with different logic.
slots.deliverable: A table with custom conditional formatting rules you set yourself, and a report page with at least one visual-level and one page-level filter configured.

slots.practicalActivity: Edit visual interactions between two visuals on a page (change one from filter to highlight), then set up a drill-down hierarchy (Year > Quarter > Month) on a chart and a drillthrough page that opens filtered to a selected Country.
slots.deliverable: A page with customized visual interactions plus a working drill-down hierarchy and a functioning drillthrough page.

slots.practicalActivity: Add 2 buttons wired to bookmarks that toggle between two different views of the same page (e.g. a 'Summary' vs. 'Detail' bookmark state), then add a trend line or forecast to an existing chart using a forecast length you choose yourself.
slots.deliverable: 2 working bookmark-driven buttons that toggle report state, plus a chart with a trend/forecast line configured with a custom forecast length.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original, fully interactive report page combining at least 6 techniques from this chapter without lesson guidance: your own visual choices, conditional formatting, a working filter, customized interactions, a drillthrough, and a bookmark-driven button.
slots.deliverable: A single polished report page demonstrating at least 6 distinct Chapter 7 techniques working together, built from your own design decisions.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page business requirements brief for an invented stakeholder (e.g. 'VP of Sales wants to track regional performance'), listing their top 3 questions, then choose and justify 4 specific KPIs that answer those questions using fields already in your model.
slots.deliverable: A written requirements brief with 3 stakeholder questions and a justified list of 4 KPIs mapped to your data model's fields.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch a dashboard wireframe (paper or a simple drawing tool) applying visual hierarchy principles (most important KPI top-left, F-pattern reading order), then write a 3-sentence 'data story' narrative your dashboard should tell a viewer at a glance.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard wireframe sketch with annotated visual hierarchy, plus a written 3-sentence narrative statement for the dashboard.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the executive dashboard your wireframe describes: one page, 4-6 visuals max, a consistent color theme, and your 4 chosen KPIs prominent at the top, following the visual hierarchy you planned.
slots.deliverable: A finished, polished one-page executive dashboard .pbix matching your own wireframe and KPI selections from the previous slot.

slots.practicalActivity: If you have access to a Power BI Service account (a free trial is enough), sign in and compare the Service web UI to Desktop side by side, listing 5 things you can only do in one or the other. Research which license tier (Free, Pro, Premium/Fabric capacity) your scenario would need and justify the choice.
slots.deliverable: A written 5-item comparison list (Desktop-only vs. Service-only capabilities) and a one-paragraph license recommendation with reasoning.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new workspace in Power BI Service (or write out the exact steps if no license is available), then publish your Chapter 8 executive dashboard .pbix to that workspace using Desktop's Publish button.
slots.deliverable: Your executive dashboard report live in a Power BI Service workspace, or a detailed step-by-step walkthrough document if publishing isn't available in your environment.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Service, locate the semantic model (dataset) behind your published report and review its settings, then share the report under a test scenario (e.g. a view-only link or a simulated colleague) and configure its access permissions.
slots.deliverable: A documented semantic model settings review plus a configured sharing/permissions setup for your published report.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Power BI App from your workspace (or document the steps), then create a standalone Service dashboard by pinning 3 tiles from your report to it, including at least one tile pinned as a live-updating tile.
slots.deliverable: A Power BI App containing your workspace content, and a Service dashboard with 3 pinned tiles from your report.

slots.practicalActivity: Diagram (in writing or a simple flowchart) how refresh works end to end for an Import-mode dataset: source change → gateway → Service → report. If you have a local data source and gateway access, install and register the on-premises data gateway.
slots.deliverable: A written refresh-flow diagram/explanation, plus a registered data gateway if your environment allows it, or documented installation steps if it doesn't.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure a scheduled refresh (e.g. daily) for your published dataset in the Service, then deliberately break the refresh (point it to a renamed/missing file or revoke a credential) and use the Service's refresh history and error message to diagnose it.
slots.deliverable: A configured scheduled refresh setting, plus a written troubleshooting log describing one real or simulated refresh failure and how you diagnosed its cause.

slots.practicalActivity: On your star-schema model, create 2 original RLS roles (not copying the lesson's example roles) that each restrict the fact table to a different Country or Segment using a DAX filter expression you write yourself.
slots.deliverable: 2 working RLS roles defined in Modeling > Manage Roles, each with your own DAX filter condition, tested using 'View As Roles' in Desktop.

slots.practicalActivity: Publish your model with RLS roles to the Service and assign a test role to a user or group (or document the exact steps if you lack admin access), then convert one static role into a dynamic RLS role driven by USERPRINCIPALNAME() against a user-mapping table you build.
slots.deliverable: A dynamic RLS role using USERPRINCIPALNAME() tested with 'View As Roles', plus documented or completed steps for assigning roles to users in the Service.

slots.practicalActivity: Apply your dynamic RLS role to a more complex scenario: a table 2 relationship-hops away from the user-mapping table, and verify the filter still correctly propagates, adjusting bidirectional filtering or adding a bridge table as needed.
slots.deliverable: A verified RLS test case where the security filter correctly restricts data on a table that isn't directly related to the security table, with a written note on what you had to change in the model.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original RLS scenario end to end without lesson guidance: design a new role, write its DAX filter, test it with View As, and document how it would behave once published to the Service for a real team you invent.
slots.deliverable: One fully original, tested RLS role with written documentation of its design rationale and expected Service behavior.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short requirements document for your capstone dashboard (pick a scenario, e.g. a regional sales performance dashboard), listing the stakeholder, their top 3 questions, and required KPIs. Then import the raw data you'll use (a multi-table dataset with at least orders, products, customers, and dates).
slots.deliverable: A written capstone requirements brief, plus all raw source tables successfully loaded into a new .pbix ('12-capstone.pbix').

slots.practicalActivity: In Power Query, clean and transform every raw table (fix data types, remove errors, handle blanks), then build a proper star schema in Model view with one fact table and the appropriate dimension tables, setting relationships and cardinality deliberately.
slots.deliverable: A cleaned set of queries and a complete star-schema data model in the capstone .pbix, verified in Model view.

slots.practicalActivity: Continue building: add a Date table to the capstone model (via CALENDAR/CALENDARAUTO), relate it properly, and double-check every relationship's cardinality and filter direction before moving on to DAX.
slots.deliverable: A capstone model with a working, related Date table and a fully reviewed relationship diagram with no unintended many-to-many or inactive relationships.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the core DAX measures your requirements brief calls for (at least 6: a few basic aggregations, at least one CALCULATE-based measure, and one time-intelligence measure), then build the main report page with the primary visuals needed to answer your stakeholder's top 3 questions.
slots.deliverable: At least 6 working, original DAX measures and a report page with the primary visuals answering the stated business questions.

slots.practicalActivity: Polish the report: apply consistent formatting and a color theme, add conditional formatting to at least one visual, and clean up titles, labels, and tooltips so the page reads clearly to someone seeing it for the first time.
slots.deliverable: A visually polished report page with consistent formatting, conditional formatting on at least one visual, and clear titles/labels.

slots.practicalActivity: Add interactivity to the capstone report (a drillthrough page, a bookmark-driven toggle, or a drill-down hierarchy matching your requirements), then publish the finished report to a Power BI Service workspace (or document the exact publish steps if unavailable).
slots.deliverable: A capstone report with at least one interactivity feature, published to the Service or with documented publish steps completed.

slots.practicalActivity: QA pass: test every measure and visual against at least 2 known filter combinations and manually verify the numbers are correct, then test the published report's refresh and confirm the data source credentials and refresh schedule are configured.
slots.deliverable: A written QA checklist with at least 4 verified test cases, and a confirmed scheduled refresh configuration on the published dataset.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure RLS on the capstone model matching your stakeholder scenario (e.g. restrict a regional manager role to their region) and confirm the scheduled refresh still works with security applied, then prepare and rehearse a 5-minute presentation of the final dashboard.
slots.deliverable: A working RLS role applied to the capstone model with refresh still functioning, plus presentation notes for a 5-minute final dashboard walkthrough.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliver the final presentation of your capstone dashboard (to a peer, mentor, or recorded for yourself): walk through the business requirement, the data model decisions, the key DAX measures, and the finished dashboard, then note 2 things you'd improve with more time.
slots.deliverable: A completed capstone presentation (live or recorded) covering requirements, model, measures, and final dashboard, plus a written list of 2 concrete improvements for a 'v2'.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can independently connect to and clean real business data in Power Query, build a proper star-schema data model, write their own DAX measures and time-intelligence calculations, and design, publish, secure, and present a polished, interactive Power BI dashboard end to end.
